hints: Focus on the clue word peptidoglycan. Ask yourself, which group of organisms is famous for having this in their cell walls?
Compare the four cell types: a plant leaf cell, a cholera bacterium, a malaria parasite, and a human blood vessel cell. Only one of these is a prokaryotic bacterial cell with a peptidoglycan wall.
walkthrough:
**Recall what peptidoglycan is**

Think of peptidoglycan as the bacterial wall molecule. It is a polymer of sugars and amino acids found only in prokaryotic bacterial cell walls.

Simple rule:
$$\text{presence of peptidoglycan} = \text{bacterial cell}$$

**Sort the cells into prokaryotic and eukaryotic**

Palisade mesophyll cells are plant cells with cellulose walls. Plasmodium falciparum is a eukaryotic protoctist parasite with no wall. Endothelial cells are animal cells with only a cell surface membrane.

Vibrio cholerae is different. The name in italics tells you it is a bacterium, so it is a prokaryote.

**Link staining to the answer**

Crystal violet stains peptidoglycan purple. Since only Vibrio cholerae cells contain peptidoglycan, only they will stain purple. That points straight to option B.

options.A: False. Palisade mesophyll cells are plant cells with cellulose cell walls, not peptidoglycan, so they will not stain purple.
options.B: Correct. Vibrio cholerae cells are bacterial cells, so their walls contain peptidoglycan which stains purple with crystal violet.
options.C: False. Plasmodium falciparum cells are eukaryotic parasite cells with no peptidoglycan wall, so they will not stain purple.
options.D: False. Endothelial cells are animal cells with no cell wall at all, so they contain no peptidoglycan to stain.
